formulations.name: Relative \(L_2\) field error
formulations.meaning: Normalizes the global field error by the reference-field magnitude.
formulations.purpose: Provides a scale-aware accuracy measure for PDE fields.
formulations.relation: It evaluates prediction quality independently of the training residual.

formulations.name: Root-mean-square error
formulations.meaning: Computes the square root of mean squared prediction error.
formulations.relation: It complements normalized norms when absolute error magnitude matters.

formulations.name: Mean absolute error
formulations.meaning: Measures the average absolute prediction discrepancy.
formulations.purpose: Provides an error statistic less dominated by large deviations than squared-error metrics.
formulations.relation: It is a complementary reference-based metric.
formulations.symbols: \(\|\cdot\|_1\): absolute value for scalars or componentwise \(L_1\) norm for vectors.

formulations.name: Maximum / \(L_\infty\) error
formulations.meaning: Reports the largest evaluated pointwise deviation.
formulations.purpose: Detects localized worst-case errors that global averages can hide.
formulations.relation: It strengthens validation for boundaries, interfaces, fronts, and singular regions.

formulations.name: Relative \(H^1\) error
formulations.meaning: Measures both field and first-derivative discrepancies.
formulations.purpose: Evaluates derivative/flux fidelity in problems where pointwise field error is insufficient.
formulations.relation: It aligns evaluation with weak, variational, and transport formulations.

formulations.name: Physics-residual RMS
formulations.meaning: Summarizes governing-equation violation on a residual evaluation set.
formulations.purpose: Measures physical consistency in the same residual sense used during training.
formulations.relation: It must not be interpreted as identical to solution error.

formulations.name: Global conservation imbalance
formulations.meaning: Measures mismatch in the integral conservation balance.
formulations.purpose: Tests physical integrity that may remain poor even when field error or pointwise residual is small.
formulations.relation: It is deliberately separate from prediction and residual metrics.

formulations.name: Relative inverse-parameter error
formulations.meaning: Quantifies error in inferred physical parameters.
formulations.purpose: Separates inverse-identification quality from state-field accuracy.
formulations.relation: It is required because a plausible state can coexist with biased inferred parameters.

formulations.name: Accuracy-matched computational speedup
formulations.meaning: Compares computational time only after requiring both methods to meet a stated accuracy threshold.
formulations.purpose: Prevents misleading speedup claims based on unequal solution quality.
formulations.relation: It belongs to computational evaluation alongside training/inference cost, memory, and hardware reporting.
formulations.symbols: \(\varepsilon^\star\): required accuracy; \(T_{\mathrm{baseline}}\), \(T_{\mathrm{PINN}}\): time-to-solution under that criterion.
